supported_distribution_findings: The generated [0,1)m/s band is slightly overrepresented relative to matched GT in both GEN repeats. These data do not support a missing-low-speed-mass diagnosis for this final baseline.
Generated speed mass above the genuine15m/s and20m/s bin boundaries is underrepresented; speed JSD can remain small while sparse tails differ appreciably in relative terms.

Length has excess mass in central4.5–5.0m bins and underrepresented long-vehicle tails at genuine6m/8m/12m bin boundaries. Width is overconcentrated near2.0–2.1m and underrepresented above genuine2.4m/2.6m/3m bin boundaries.

The scalar-speed physical output clamps negatives to zero. This can put mass into the first1m/s bin, but aggregate histograms cannot separate exact zero, positive0–1m/s values, or quantify preclamp negatives; this is a source-based possibility, not demonstrated causality.

Generated type predictions define the vehicle population. Attribute histogram differences reflect both physical-state generation and which rows are predicted as vehicles; these exports do not provide an ego/non-ego or GT-type-conditioned decomposition.
resolution_and_tail_limits: No exact stationary(speed=0) fraction or thresholds below1m/s can be obtained from these speed bins. Label [0,1)m/s as low speed, not stationary.
Clipping places all speed>=50m/s, length>=25m, and width>=5m into the corresponding final bin. Final-bin counts cannot distinguish above-range outliers from values inside that bin.
Sparse-tail counts, two generation repeats, and one trained seed do not establish statistical robustness or eventual128epoch behavior.

The shape mode is linear. Positive final outputs are not guaranteed by exp, and generated dimension values are not silently deleted by the current initial-scene metric path. Counts in the first clipping bin cannot distinguish nonpositive values from physically small positive values.

metric_population_and_definitions.vehicle_population: SMART generated type0 rows. Pedestrians1 and cyclists2 are excluded from all seven vehicle metrics. No generated GT-validity/FOV/offroad deletion is applied. Optional initial_valid is supported by the evaluator, but current InitDiffusion SMART._rollouts output does not emit this field.
metric_population_and_definitions.invalid_size_policy: mask is used in input/training handling of invalid log-size annotations, not as an inference-time generated-size filter. Baseline uses linear size; get_output forwards predicted shape with exact fixed ego shape overrides. The current initial-scene path emits no initial_valid and does not mask generated shapes.
metric_population_and_definitions.collision_population: All retained generated vehicles, including offroad vehicles and ego if type0; no onroad subset restriction. One snapshot, not a trajectory collision metric or a pair count.
metric_population_and_definitions.collision_geometry: Five circle centers along each oriented vehicle length, with center extent from -length/2+width/2 to length/2-width/2. Count a vehicle once if any of the25 circle pair distances to another vehicle is strictly <(width_j+width_k)/sqrt(3.8).
metric_population_and_definitions.collision_aggregation: Sum integer vehicle counts involved in >=1 overlap across scenes / sum vehicle counts *100percent. A pair normally contributes two vehicles. This is not the mean of scene-level rates.
metric_population_and_definitions.onroad: Vehicle centroid minimum Euclidean distance to all points of compact official centerlines resampled to100points is <=1.5m. This is not a drivable-polygon or vehicle-footprint criterion.
metric_population_and_definitions.lat: Only onroad vehicles. Minimum Euclidean distance to resampled centerline points in metres, unsigned; not exact perpendicular distance to continuous segments. Normalize its histogram by the onroad feature count.
metric_population_and_definitions.angle: Only onroad vehicles. Vehicle heading minus heading of the segment immediately preceding the nearest centerline point (nearest index clamped to1..last), wrapped with atan2(sinDelta,cosDelta), converted to degrees; histogram uses5degree bins.
metric_population_and_definitions.lat_angle_denominator_warning: Offroad vehicles are excluded from lat/angle histograms but remain in L/W/speed/collision. A lower lat JSD alone does not establish more onroad coverage. Report generated_onroad_fraction separately.
metric_population_and_definitions.nearest_distance: All vehicle centroids in scenes with>1vehicles, excluding self; singleton scenes contribute no value. Includes ego as candidate and as neighbor.
metric_population_and_definitions.attributes: Length,width,speed use all retained generated vehicle rows irrespective of onroad status. Speed is instantaneous velocity norm, not finite-difference trajectory speed.
metric_population_and_definitions.ego_inclusion: No metric exclusion for ego. Fixed GT position,heading,shape,type of vehicle ego contribute to nearest/shape/speed/collision and lat/angle when onroad. Ego speed remains generated because fix_ego_velocity=false. Fixed ego pose contributes GT-conditioned mass, so aggregate JSD is not a non-ego-only generation score.
metric_population_and_definitions.ego_attribution_limit: These aggregated histograms do not expose ego-specific counts or histograms. Do not assign a particular shape peak wholly to ego or claim an exact4096ego histogram count without an additional per-scene ego decomposition.
metric_population_and_definitions.GT_population: Cached GT conversion selects original agent_types argmax vehicle0, including ego without ego-mask exclusion. Baseline matched reference mode uses exactly the same4096filenames for both GEN repeats.
metric_population_and_definitions.score_units: JSDs are dimensionless natural-log divergence: scipy JensenShannonDistance squared, near/lat *10; angle/length/width/speed *100. Collision is percentage. Physical feature units are not score units.
